raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On gfx1151 (Strix Halo, RDNA 3.5, 20 CU) a bs=1 decode step is almost entirely single-row GEMV (`x[1,K] @ W[N,K].T`). rocBLAS serves that as a tiled GEMM with a 96-row tile, so the number of CTAs that can be resident is pinned by `N/96`: 32-64 CTAs for the dense projections of a 0.6B-9B model. On 20 compute units that is not enough to cover memory latency, and the measured read bandwidth is 45-93 GB/s, i.e. 20-40% of what the part can reach.

Splitting K gives every k-chunk its own CTA group. At M=1 the fp32 partials are `N * 4 B * split_k`, 0.2-0.4% of the weight bytes, so the extra traffic is negligible next to the 2-4x occupancy gain.

Two kernels: one CTA per (32-wide n-tile, 512-wide k-chunk) accumulating in fp32 and storing partials, then a reduce kernel with a static order that stores bf16. `tl.dot` is deliberately not used — at M=1 it requires 16 rows and spends 15/16 of the loaded weight tile on padding (76 GB/s vs 202 GB/s on `4096x1024`).

## Modifications

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/rdna_small_m_gemv.py` (new) | split-K kernel (`BN=32` / `BK=512` / fp32 partials) + fixed-order reduce + gate (incl. HIP `< 7.3`) + `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV` |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py` | route `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` to the kernel on the eager path (+ module globals injected in `initialize_bf16_gemm_config`) |
| `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py` | `is_gfx1151_supported()`, alongside the other arch predicates |
| `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` | `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV` kill switch in the ROCm section |
| `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py` | `KernelSpec` entry for the new op |
| `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_rdna_small_m_gemv.py` (new) | gate accept/reject matrix (incl. the HIP bound), numeric parity vs fp32 and rocBLAS, batch invariance; registered on AMD CI |

The gate is `gfx1151` + HIP `< 7.3` + `M==1` + bf16 + contiguous + `n % 32 == 0` + `k % 512 == 0` + `2 <= k/512 <= 64` + `N/32 <= 1024`. Both bounds are measured rather than guessed: a `34816x5120` gate_up (1088 n-tiles) reaches 145.7 GB/s via rocBLAS and only 133.0 GB/s with split-K, so the crossover sits at the n-tile bound, and `split_k` up to 50 was still winning (1.27x on `5120x25600`) when the old cap was 32.

The HIP bound is there because the compared baseline moves with the stack: the constants beat the `F.linear` of ROCm 7.2.x (74-135 GB/s on the gated shapes), while on 7.13 the same call reaches 205-242 GB/s and split-K loses on every gated shape (numbers in the section below). We can only run 7.2.x here, so the wide routing stops at the last generation we measured instead of extrapolating; the bound is a single constant, so it can be raised once a newer stack has its own shape-level numbers, and `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV` still turns the path off outright.

Compiled graphs keep the GEMM: a raw Triton launch cannot be traced, so the branch is skipped under `torch.compiler.is_compiling()`.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy eval was run (the target box has no network for GSM8K). The evidence is numeric instead, against an fp32 reference on the 4B/27B decode shapes:

| n x k | split_k | split-K max abs | rocBLAS max abs | bf16 store step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10240x2560 | 5 | 0.03125 | 0.03125 | 0.02098 |
| 18432x2560 | 5 | 0.03037 | 0.03037 | 0.01988 |
| 2560x9216 | 18 | 0.06160 | 0.06160 | 0.03479 |
| 5120x17408 | 34 | 0.06234 | 0.06266 | 0.05103 |

Both paths land on the same one-ulp-of-bf16 bound from the final store, so this is not an accumulation regression. Accumulation is fp32 and the reduction order is static, so the kernel is batch-invariant (covered by `test_batch_invariant`).

One caveat: a greedy 24-token decode is **not** bit-identical to rocBLAS. On the 4B, one of two prompts diverged around token 20 (`...is NOT a characteristic` vs `...is NOT a reason`) — a tie-break flip at ~1 ulp of logits, not a computation error.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

gfx1151, bs=1. Two levels of measurement, because they answer different questions.

**Kernel level** — per-shape cold-weight microbenchmarks (200 MB working set, far beyond the 2 MB L2), sglang's actual fused projection shapes:

| Shape | split_k | rocBLAS GB/s | split-K GB/s | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6B qkv 4096x1024 | 2 | 55.0 | 201.6 | 3.67x |
| 0.6B gate_up 6144x1024 | 2 | 51.6 | 212.7 | 4.12x |
| 0.6B down 1024x3072 | 6 | 92.5 | 195.5 | 2.11x |
| 4B qkv 10240x2560 | 5 | 120.5 | 173.4 | 1.44x |
| 4B o_proj 2560x4096 | 8 | 74.2 | 196.6 | 2.65x |
| 4B down 2560x9216 | 18 | 134.8 | 220.5 | 1.64x |

**End to end, bs=1** — same overlay, only `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV` differs:

| Harness | rocBLAS | split-K | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original measurement in this PR, Qwen3-0.6B (8 runs, median) | 22.7 ms/token (43.99 tok/s) | 13.7 ms/token (73.03 tok/s) | 1.66x |
| Original measurement in this PR, Qwen3.5-4B (8 runs, median) | 69.2 ms/token (14.44 tok/s) | 51.5 ms/token (19.43 tok/s) | 1.34x |
| `bench_serving`, Qwen3-0.6B, random 1024 in / 256 out, 8 prompts at c=1, Triton attention, decode CUDA graphs on (independent run, thanks @twoask) | 16.99 ms TPOT (58.1 tok/s) | 15.78 ms TPOT (62.4 tok/s) | +7.5% TPOT, +7.4% throughput |

The rows use different harnesses and therefore different baselines — compare within a row, not across. The per-shape table is the harness-independent part, and it is what the gate is tuned against.

For reference, @twoask measured #46327's weight padding in the same serving harness at 16.98 -> 14.66 ms TPOT (+15.9%), so padding and split-K are complementary rather than additive.

Why the kernel is capped on this part (independent sweep by @twoask): on aliased rows (K\*2 a multiple of 2 KiB) split-K bandwidth is about 31 / 62 / 120 GB/s at `BLOCK_K` = 256 / 512 / 1024 regardless of `BLOCK_N` and warps — each CTA reads 32 rows that are 8 KiB apart, which lands on a single channel. Padded rows reach 190-218 GB/s, which is the gap #46327 addresses.

**Where the gain stops: newer ROCm stacks.** Independent runs by @twoask on ROCm 7.13 / torch 2.10.0+rocm7.13 / Triton 3.6, at head `895c4a4950`, in the same 4B `bench_serving` harness as the 0.6B row above:

| Arm | Median TPOT | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| split-K off | 47.67 / 48.07 ms | 20.3 |
| split-K on | 52.38 / 52.50 ms (-9.7%) | 18.6 |
| #46327 padding off | 47.81 / 47.79 ms | 20.3 |
| #46327 padding on | 44.10 / 44.07 ms (+8.4%) | 22.0 |

Their per-shape numbers say why: on that stack `F.linear` already reads the K=2560 rows at 205-232 GB/s while split-K tops out at 195-199 (0.86-0.95x), and the aliased K=4096 rows only tie (0.96x); the 0.6B model still gains because all of its rows are K=1024. The 7.2.x baseline on the same 4B qkv shape is 120.5 GB/s — the 1.44x row in the table above — so the delta is the stack, not the shape. That is what the HIP `< 7.3` gate encodes: the 7.2.x gains are kept, and a 7.13 runner falls back to its faster stock GEMM instead of taking a 9.7% TPOT regression.

## Not covered (please weigh these before merging)

- The gate is exact to `gfx1151` because all constants were measured on the 20-CU part. Wider RDNA parts (gfx1100 etc.) have enough CTAs that the rocBLAS tile already saturates; broadening needs their own measurements.
- TP>1 mostly falls out of the gate: row-parallel K shards stop being multiples of 512 (e.g. 4B down at TP=4 is k=2304). No multi-GPU numbers.
- Qwen3.8-27B was not run end-to-end: its 54 GB of bf16 weights exceed this machine's ~47 GiB GTT limit, so the only 27B evidence is the per-shape microbenchmarks and one numeric-parity row.
- gfx1151 has no CI runner, so the numeric tests run on whatever ROCm device AMD CI has (the kernel is plain Triton, arch-agnostic); the gate tests are arch-pinned and run anywhere.
- Stacks at or above HIP 7.3 are gated off rather than re-tuned: the only end-to-end evidence there is @twoask's (0.6B +7.5%, 4B -9.7%), and the aliased `K=1024` rows that still win would need their own shape-level sweep before a narrower rule is worth adding.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — speed results are above; accuracy is numeric parity against an fp32 reference, no GSM8K eval was run on this offline box.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no page documents kernel-level env switches yet; the new switch is documented in `environ.py` next to the other ROCm ones.

Verification on gfx1151 (ROCm 7.2.4 / torch 2.9.1 / Triton 3.7): `pytest test_rdna_small_m_gemv.py -q` -> 11 passed, 15 subtests, 3.9 s (registered `est_time=20`, `stage-b`, `1-gpu-small-amd`).

- In-process, interleaved A/B/C on one GPU.
- M=1, bf16, Qwen3-8B projection shapes.
- Each arm rotates over ≥1 GiB of distinct weight copies so every call streams from DRAM (the 64–96 MB last-level cache otherwise inflates bandwidth).
- 11 rounds; medians reported.
- Arms: `F.linear` on a plain weight; `F.linear` on #46327's padded row stride (+128 B); and this PR's `rdna_splitk_gemv` with its own gate, forced on since the gate is gfx1151-only.
- Max relative error vs fp32 is identical across arms on both GPUs.

**RDNA3, gfx1100 (W7900-class, torch 2.13)** — GB/s, speedup vs plain:

| shape (K -> N) | plain | padded (#46327) | split-K (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| qkv 4096 -> 6144 | 355 | 448 (1.26x) | **510 (1.44x)** |
| o 4096 -> 4096 | 320 | 392 (1.23x) | **595 (1.86x)** |
| gate_up 4096 -> 24576 | 377 | **516 (1.37x)** | 420 (1.12x) |
| down 12288 -> 4096 | 402 | 451 (1.12x) | **580 (1.45x)** |
| lm_head 4096 -> 151936 | 646 | **694 (1.07x)** | outside the gate |

**RDNA4, gfx1201 (R9700, torch 2.10)**:

| shape (K -> N) | plain | padded (#46327) | split-K (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| qkv 4096 -> 6144 | 471 | 494 (1.05x) | **567 (1.21x)** |
| o 4096 -> 4096 | 445 | 433 (0.97x) | **553 (1.24x)** |

| down 12288 -> 4096 | 477 | 525 (1.10x) | **595 (1.25x)** |
| lm_head 4096 -> 151936 | 560 | 561 (1.00x) | outside the gate |

Observations (just data, not a verdict):

1. Split-K helps well beyond gfx1151. It is the fastest arm on 3 of 4 gated shapes on gfx1100, and on all 4 on gfx1201. Widening the gate to `gfx11*`/`gfx120*` looks worthwhile.
2. On gfx1100, padding still wins on the wide `gate_up` and on `lm_head`, which is outside the split-K gate. So the two mechanisms are complementary rather than redundant.
3. As written they don't compose. Padded weights are non-contiguous, so this kernel would never fire after #46327. One option: let the split-K kernel accept a row stride (it reads rows anyway), so padding plus split-K can stack. Another: pad only weights the split-K gate rejects.

cc @twoask (#46327). The end-to-end decode numbers for padding on gfx1100 are in my comment on that PR.

@Woody-Hu @vivienfanghuagood here's the same comparison on gfx1151, since that's the arch this PR gates on. I got quite different results from the numbers in the description, so I'd love to figure out what's different between our setups.

**Setup:**
- Hardware: gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), ROCm 7.13, torch 2.10, Triton 3.6. Default hipBLASLt, no TunableOp.
- Kernels: this PR's split-K kernels at `000e19094a`, unmodified.

| Shape (N x K) | plain GB/s | padded (#46327) | split-K | split-K + padded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B qkv 6144x4096 | 150.8 | **1.41x** | 0.53x | 0.98x |

| 0.6B gate_up 6144x1024 | 127.6 | **1.64x** | 0.96x | 1.03x |
| 0.6B down 1024x3072 | 134.1 | **1.39x** | 1.19x | 1.03x |
| 4B qkv 10240x2560 | 223.9 | 1.00x (not padded) | 0.87x | 0.87x |
| 4B o 2560x4096 | 115.1 | **1.80x** | 0.96x | 1.19x |
| 4B down 2560x9216 | 204.3 | **1.08x** | 0.79x | 0.71x |

Llama-3.1-8B shapes look the same as Qwen3-8B. Max relative error vs fp32 is identical across all four arms.

**My baselines are much higher than the description's.** I timed the plain arm on both BLAS libraries:

| Shape | hipBLASLt (here) | rocBLAS (here) | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6B qkv | 126.8 | 143.3 | 55.0 |
| 0.6B gate_up | 127.8 | 132.3 | 51.6 |

**A few observations:**
- Most of the slow shapes have rows that are a multiple of 2 KiB (K = 1024, 3072, 4096, 9216), which is the gfx11 cache aliasing #46327 fixes. Split-K is hit by it too: padding takes its gate_up from 63 to 191 GB/s.
- On gfx1151 here, split-K doesn't add anything on top of padding. It does look clearly useful on gfx1100/gfx1201 going by @vivienfanghuagood's numbers.
- Either way, relaxing `is_contiguous()` to `weight.stride(1) == 1` (in both the gate in `unquant.py` and the wrapper assert) seems worth doing, so the two PRs can't silently disable each other.

Happy to rerun with your settings if you can share them.

Follow-up with two more checks on gfx1151.

**End to end, Qwen3-0.6B, bs=1.** I used this PR's head with `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV=1/0`, and #46327 with `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX11_WEIGHT_PADDING=1/0`. **Why the kernel is slow here.** I swept `BLOCK_N` x `BLOCK_K` x `num_warps` on plain and padded weights:

- **Aliasing caps it.** On aliased rows (K*2 a multiple of 2 KiB), split-K's bandwidth depends almost only on `BLOCK_K`. - **The tile isn't the best for this compiler.** On an unaliased shape (4B qkv, K=2560), the default 32x512 / 4 warps (106 VGPRs) gives 198 GB/s. 8x512 / 8 warps gives 229 GB/s, slightly above `F.linear`'s 223 GB/s. The larger tiles hit 256 VGPRs and spill.

Your unit tests all pass here (10/10), so this is about speed only, not correctness. I'd still be curious what your ROCm / torch / Triton versions and power mode are, since your baselines are roughly 2x lower than mine.

Thanks — that pins it down.

**Our stack is older, so I cannot re-run your `F.linear` numbers here**: `torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4.git39497456`, `torch.version.hip = 7.2.53211-97f5574fe2`, Triton 3.7.0, gfx1151 — ROCm 7.2.4 vs your 7.13. **Change pushed** (`a4966b9`): the gate now also requires `get_hip_version() < (7, 3)`, via `_BASELINE_CROSSOVER_HIP_VERSION`, with the reason recorded next to the constant. detail.body:
## Motivation

On gfx1151 (Strix Halo, RDNA 3.5, 20 CU) a bs=1 decode step is almost entirely single-row GEMV (`x[1,K] @ W[N,K].T`). rocBLAS serves that as a tiled GEMM with a 96-row tile, so the number of CTAs that can be resident is pinned by `N/96`: 32-64 CTAs for the dense projections of a 0.6B-9B model. On 20 compute units that is not enough to cover memory latency, and the measured read bandwidth is 45-93 GB/s, i.e. 20-40% of what the part can reach.

Splitting K gives every k-chunk its own CTA group. At M=1 the fp32 partials are `N * 4 B * split_k`, 0.2-0.4% of the weight bytes, so the extra traffic is negligible next to the 2-4x occupancy gain.

Two kernels: one CTA per (32-wide n-tile, 512-wide k-chunk) accumulating in fp32 and storing partials, then a reduce kernel with a static order that stores bf16. `tl.dot` is deliberately not used — at M=1 it requires 16 rows and spends 15/16 of the loaded weight tile on padding (76 GB/s vs 202 GB/s on `4096x1024`).

## Modifications

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/rdna_small_m_gemv.py` (new) | split-K kernel (`BN=32` / `BK=512` / fp32 partials) + fixed-order reduce + gate (incl. HIP `< 7.3`) + `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV` |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py` | route `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` to the kernel on the eager path (+ module globals injected in `initialize_bf16_gemm_config`) |
| `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py` | `is_gfx1151_supported()`, alongside the other arch predicates |
| `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` | `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV` kill switch in the ROCm section |
| `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/__init__.py` | `KernelSpec` entry for the new op |
| `test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_rdna_small_m_gemv.py` (new) | gate accept/reject matrix (incl. the HIP bound), numeric parity vs fp32 and rocBLAS, batch invariance; registered on AMD CI |

The gate is `gfx1151` + HIP `< 7.3` + `M==1` + bf16 + contiguous + `n % 32 == 0` + `k % 512 == 0` + `2 <= k/512 <= 64` + `N/32 <= 1024`. Both bounds are measured rather than guessed: a `34816x5120` gate_up (1088 n-tiles) reaches 145.7 GB/s via rocBLAS and only 133.0 GB/s with split-K, so the crossover sits at the n-tile bound, and `split_k` up to 50 was still winning (1.27x on `5120x25600`) when the old cap was 32.

The HIP bound is there because the compared baseline moves with the stack: the constants beat the `F.linear` of ROCm 7.2.x (74-135 GB/s on the gated shapes), while on 7.13 the same call reaches 205-242 GB/s and split-K loses on every gated shape (numbers in the section below). We can only run 7.2.x here, so the wide routing stops at the last generation we measured instead of extrapolating; the bound is a single constant, so it can be raised once a newer stack has its own shape-level numbers, and `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV` still turns the path off outright.

Compiled graphs keep the GEMM: a raw Triton launch cannot be traced, so the branch is skipped under `torch.compiler.is_compiling()`.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy eval was run (the target box has no network for GSM8K). The evidence is numeric instead, against an fp32 reference on the 4B/27B decode shapes:

| n x k | split_k | split-K max abs | rocBLAS max abs | bf16 store step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10240x2560 | 5 | 0.03125 | 0.03125 | 0.02098 |
| 18432x2560 | 5 | 0.03037 | 0.03037 | 0.01988 |
| 2560x9216 | 18 | 0.06160 | 0.06160 | 0.03479 |
| 5120x17408 | 34 | 0.06234 | 0.06266 | 0.05103 |

Both paths land on the same one-ulp-of-bf16 bound from the final store, so this is not an accumulation regression. Accumulation is fp32 and the reduction order is static, so the kernel is batch-invariant (covered by `test_batch_invariant`).

One caveat: a greedy 24-token decode is **not** bit-identical to rocBLAS. On the 4B, one of two prompts diverged around token 20 (`...is NOT a characteristic` vs `...is NOT a reason`) — a tie-break flip at ~1 ulp of logits, not a computation error.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

gfx1151, bs=1. Two levels of measurement, because they answer different questions.

**Kernel level** — per-shape cold-weight microbenchmarks (200 MB working set, far beyond the 2 MB L2), sglang's actual fused projection shapes:

| Shape | split_k | rocBLAS GB/s | split-K GB/s | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6B qkv 4096x1024 | 2 | 55.0 | 201.6 | 3.67x |
| 0.6B gate_up 6144x1024 | 2 | 51.6 | 212.7 | 4.12x |
| 0.6B down 1024x3072 | 6 | 92.5 | 195.5 | 2.11x |
| 4B qkv 10240x2560 | 5 | 120.5 | 173.4 | 1.44x |
| 4B o_proj 2560x4096 | 8 | 74.2 | 196.6 | 2.65x |
| 4B down 2560x9216 | 18 | 134.8 | 220.5 | 1.64x |

**End to end, bs=1** — same overlay, only `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV` differs:

| Harness | rocBLAS | split-K | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original measurement in this PR, Qwen3-0.6B (8 runs, median) | 22.7 ms/token (43.99 tok/s) | 13.7 ms/token (73.03 tok/s) | 1.66x |
| Original measurement in this PR, Qwen3.5-4B (8 runs, median) | 69.2 ms/token (14.44 tok/s) | 51.5 ms/token (19.43 tok/s) | 1.34x |
| `bench_serving`, Qwen3-0.6B, random 1024 in / 256 out, 8 prompts at c=1, Triton attention, decode CUDA graphs on (independent run, thanks @twoask) | 16.99 ms TPOT (58.1 tok/s) | 15.78 ms TPOT (62.4 tok/s) | +7.5% TPOT, +7.4% throughput |

The rows use different harnesses and therefore different baselines — compare within a row, not across. The per-shape table is the harness-independent part, and it is what the gate is tuned against.

For reference, @twoask measured #46327's weight padding in the same serving harness at 16.98 -> 14.66 ms TPOT (+15.9%), so padding and split-K are complementary rather than additive.

Why the kernel is capped on this part (independent sweep by @twoask): on aliased rows (K\*2 a multiple of 2 KiB) split-K bandwidth is about 31 / 62 / 120 GB/s at `BLOCK_K` = 256 / 512 / 1024 regardless of `BLOCK_N` and warps — each CTA reads 32 rows that are 8 KiB apart, which lands on a single channel. Padded rows reach 190-218 GB/s, which is the gap #46327 addresses.

**Where the gain stops: newer ROCm stacks.** Independent runs by @twoask on ROCm 7.13 / torch 2.10.0+rocm7.13 / Triton 3.6, at head `895c4a4950`, in the same 4B `bench_serving` harness as the 0.6B row above:

| Arm | Median TPOT | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| split-K off | 47.67 / 48.07 ms | 20.3 |
| split-K on | 52.38 / 52.50 ms (-9.7%) | 18.6 |
| #46327 padding off | 47.81 / 47.79 ms | 20.3 |
| #46327 padding on | 44.10 / 44.07 ms (+8.4%) | 22.0 |

Their per-shape numbers say why: on that stack `F.linear` already reads the K=2560 rows at 205-232 GB/s while split-K tops out at 195-199 (0.86-0.95x), and the aliased K=4096 rows only tie (0.96x); the 0.6B model still gains because all of its rows are K=1024. The 7.2.x baseline on the same 4B qkv shape is 120.5 GB/s — the 1.44x row in the table above — so the delta is the stack, not the shape. That is what the HIP `< 7.3` gate encodes: the 7.2.x gains are kept, and a 7.13 runner falls back to its faster stock GEMM instead of taking a 9.7% TPOT regression.

## Not covered (please weigh these before merging)

- The gate is exact to `gfx1151` because all constants were measured on the 20-CU part. Wider RDNA parts (gfx1100 etc.) have enough CTAs that the rocBLAS tile already saturates; broadening needs their own measurements.
- TP>1 mostly falls out of the gate: row-parallel K shards stop being multiples of 512 (e.g. 4B down at TP=4 is k=2304). No multi-GPU numbers.
- Qwen3.8-27B was not run end-to-end: its 54 GB of bf16 weights exceed this machine's ~47 GiB GTT limit, so the only 27B evidence is the per-shape microbenchmarks and one numeric-parity row.
- gfx1151 has no CI runner, so the numeric tests run on whatever ROCm device AMD CI has (the kernel is plain Triton, arch-agnostic); the gate tests are arch-pinned and run anywhere.
- Stacks at or above HIP 7.3 are gated off rather than re-tuned: the only end-to-end evidence there is @twoask's (0.6B +7.5%, 4B -9.7%), and the aliased `K=1024` rows that still win would need their own shape-level sweep before a narrower rule is worth adding.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — speed results are above; accuracy is numeric parity against an fp32 reference, no GSM8K eval was run on this offline box.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no page documents kernel-level env switches yet; the new switch is documented in `environ.py` next to the other ROCm ones.

Verification on gfx1151 (ROCm 7.2.4 / torch 2.9.1 / Triton 3.7): `pytest test_rdna_small_m_gemv.py -q` -> 11 passed, 15 subtests, 3.9 s (registered `est_time=20`, `stage-b`, `1-gpu-small-amd`).

+"""Split-K bf16 GEMV for single-row decode on RDNA APUs.
+
+Enabled on gfx1151 (Strix Halo) running the ROCm generation these constants were tuned
+on; the tuning was measured there and has not been re-measured on the wider RDNA parts,
+which have enough compute units that the rocBLAS tile already covers the machine.
+
+Motivation
+----------
+A single-row (M=1) decode projection ``x[1, K] @ W[N, K].T`` is served by rocBLAS
+as a tiled GEMM. The tile is fixed at 96 rows/columns, so the number of CTA
+groups that can run at once is pinned by ``N / 96``: for the decode projections of
+a 0.6B-9B model that is 32-64 concurrent CTAs, far below what is needed to cover
+memory latency on a 20-CU APU. Measured on gfx1151 (Strix Halo, 20 CU): 45-93 GB/s,
+i.e. 20-40% of the achievable read bandwidth.
+
+Splitting K gives every k-chunk its own CTA group. For M=1 the fp32 partials are
+``N * 4 B * split_k``, which is 0.2-0.4% of the weight bytes, so the extra traffic
+is negligible next to the 2-4x occupancy gain.
+
+Note that this kernel deliberately reduces with ``tl.sum`` instead of ``tl.dot``:
+``tl.dot`` needs at least 16 rows, so at M=1 it spends 15/16 of the loaded weight
+tile on padding and is measurably slower here (76 GB/s vs 202 GB/s on gfx1151 for
+``4096x1024``).
+
+Numerics
+--------
+Accumulation is fp32 and the K-split reduction order is static, so the result does
+not depend on the batch composition (batch-invariant).
+"""
+
+from functools import lru_cache
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.utils import get_hip_version, is_gfx1151_supported
+
+_BLOCK_N = 32
+_BLOCK_K = 512
+# Measured on gfx1151 with cold weights (200 MB working set): K splits of 8-50 all
+# beat rocBLAS (1.37x at split_k=34 for 5120x17408, 1.27x at split_k=50 for
+# 5120x25600), so the cap only guards against pathological K rather than a
+# bandwidth crossover.
+_MAX_SPLIT_K = 64
+_SUPPORTED_ROWS = 1
+# Above this many n-tiles the GEMM is already wide enough to saturate the bus, and
+# splitting K only adds the partial/reduce traffic. Measured on gfx1151 with cold
+# weights: the 151936 vocabulary head reaches 140 GB/s via rocBLAS and drops to
+# 121 GB/s with split-K; a 34816x5120 gate_up (1088 tiles) is 145.7 vs 133.0 GB/s,
+# i.e. the crossover sits right at this bound.
+_MAX_N_TILES = 1024
+# The baseline these constants beat is the stock `F.linear` of ROCm 7.2.x (74-135 GB/s
+# on the gated shapes). On ROCm 7.13 the same call reaches 205-242 GB/s and split-K
+# loses 4-21% on every gated shape, so the wide routing stays off from 7.3 onwards
+# instead of extrapolating from the older numbers. The aliased K=1024 rows still gain
+# 7.5% end to end on 7.13, but a narrower rule for them needs its own measurements.
+_BASELINE_CROSSOVER_HIP_VERSION = (7, 3)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def _baseline_is_slow() -> bool:
+    """Whether the stock BLAS baseline is still the one these constants were tuned for."""
+    return get_hip_version() < _BASELINE_CROSSOVER_HIP_VERSION
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gemv_split_k_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    w_ptr,
+    part_ptr,
+    stride_wn,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """One CTA per (n-tile, k-chunk). ``N % BLOCK_N == 0`` is guaranteed by the gate."""
+    pid_n = tl.program_id(0)
+    pid_k = tl.program_id(1)
+    offs_n = pid_n * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+    offs_k = pid_k * BLOCK_K + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
+
+    w = tl.load(w_ptr + offs_n[:, None] * stride_wn + offs_k[None, :])
+    x = tl.load(x_ptr + offs_k)
+    acc = tl.sum(w.to(tl.float32) * x[None, :].to(tl.float32), axis=1)
+    tl.store(part_ptr + pid_k * N + offs_n, acc)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _reduce_split_k_kernel(
+    part_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    SPLIT_K: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    offs = pid * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_N,), dtype=tl.float32)
+    for s in tl.static_range(SPLIT_K):
+        acc += tl.load(part_ptr + s * N + offs)
+    tl.store(out_ptr + offs, acc.to(tl.bfloat16))
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def _is_disabled() -> bool:
+    return envs.SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_RDNA_SPLITK_GEMV.get()
+
+
+def use_rdna_splitk_gemv(m: int, n: int, k: int, weight_dtype: torch.dtype) -> bool:
+    """Whether a single-row bf16 GEMV should be routed to the split-K kernel."""
+    if _is_disabled():
+        return False
+    if not _baseline_is_slow():
+        return False
+    if m != _SUPPORTED_ROWS or weight_dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+        return False
+    if n % _BLOCK_N != 0 or k % _BLOCK_K != 0:
+        return False
+    if n // _BLOCK_N > _MAX_N_TILES:
+        return False
+    split_k = k // _BLOCK_K
+    if split_k < 2 or split_k > _MAX_SPLIT_K:
+        # split_k == 1 has no occupancy problem to fix; a very large split_k turns
+        # the reduction into the bottleneck.
+        return False
+    return is_gfx1151_supported()
+
+
+def rdna_splitk_gemv(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``x[1, K] @ weight[N, K].T`` for bf16 weights, returning bf16 ``[1, N]``."""
+    n, k = weight.shape
+    split_k = k // _BLOCK_K
+    # The kernel has no tail mask: it reads one contiguous K-row per weight row and
+    # writes whole n-tiles.
+    assert (
+        weight.is_contiguous()
+        and x.numel() == k
+        and n % _BLOCK_N == 0
+        and k % _BLOCK_K == 0
+    ), (weight.shape, weight.stride(), x.shape)
+    x_flat = x.reshape(-1)
+    partial = torch.empty((split_k, n), dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    out = torch.empty((1, n), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=x.device)
+    _gemv_split_k_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, _BLOCK_N), split_k)](
+        x_flat,
+        weight,
+        partial,
+        weight.stride(0),
+        N=n,
+        BLOCK_N=_BLOCK_N,
+        BLOCK_K=_BLOCK_K,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    _reduce_split_k_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, _BLOCK_N),)](
+        partial,
+        out,
+        N=n,
+        SPLIT_K=split_k,
+        BLOCK_N=_BLOCK_N,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    return out

@@ -1105,6 +1105,9 @@ class Envs:
     SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_ROUTER = EnvBool(True)
     SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE = EnvBool(True)
     SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_PROJ = EnvBool(True)
+    # Route single-row bf16 decode projections to the RDNA split-K GEMV on

+"""Tests the RDNA split-K bf16 GEMV used for single-row decode projections on gfx1151.
+
+The shape gate is exercised on every ROCm GPU (the arch check and the ROCm generation
+are patched out, so the accept/reject rules are covered on hosts without a gfx1151 device
+running the stack the constants were tuned on); the kernel is compared against an fp32
+reference and rocBLAS on the shapes that occur in decode.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm import rdna_small_m_gemv as splitk
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_hip
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=20, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+# Shapes from a 0.6B decode step: (n, k) of qkv / o / gate_up / down.
+DECODE_SHAPES = [(4096, 1024), (1024, 2048), (6144, 1024), (1024, 3072)]
+
+
+class TestGate(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        # The gate's last condition is the gfx1151 arch check; pin it so the shape and
+        # dtype rules are testable on hosts without that device. The ROCm generation is
+        # pinned as well: the constants were tuned against the 7.2 baseline, and the gate
+        # is off from 7.3 on, so an unpinned runner would reject every accepted shape.
+        patcher = mock.patch.object(splitk, "is_gfx1151_supported", return_value=True)
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+        version_patcher = mock.patch.object(
+            splitk, "get_hip_version", return_value=(7, 2, 0)
+        )
+        version_patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(version_patcher.stop)
+        splitk._baseline_is_slow.cache_clear()
+        self.addCleanup(splitk._baseline_is_slow.cache_clear)
+
+    def test_version_gate(self):
+        # The kernel only wins against the 7.2.x baseline; on 7.13 the stock BLAS reaches
+        # 205-242 GB/s and split-K loses on every gated shape, so the wide routing stops
+        # at the last generation we measured.
+        self.assertTrue(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 4096, 1024, torch.bfloat16))
+        for version in [(7, 3, 0), (7, 13, 0), (8, 0, 0)]:
+            with self.subTest(version=version):
+                with mock.patch.object(splitk, "get_hip_version", return_value=version):
+                    splitk._baseline_is_slow.cache_clear()
+                    self.assertFalse(
+                        splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 4096, 1024, torch.bfloat16)
+                    )
+        splitk._baseline_is_slow.cache_clear()
+
+    def test_accepts_decode_shapes(self):
+        for n, k in DECODE_SHAPES:
+            with self.subTest(n=n, k=k):
+                self.assertTrue(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, n, k, torch.bfloat16))
+
+    def test_rejects_non_single_row(self):
+        # The tl.sum reduction is single-row by construction; multi-row must not
+        # silently route here.
+        self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(2, 4096, 1024, torch.bfloat16))
+        self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(64, 4096, 1024, torch.bfloat16))
+
+    def test_rejects_wide_head(self):
+        # Wide layers already saturate the bus; split-K loses there.
+        self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 151936, 1024, torch.bfloat16))
+
+    def test_accepts_large_split_k(self):
+        # 5120x17408 is a 27B down_proj: split_k=34, measured 1.37x over rocBLAS.
+        self.assertTrue(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 5120, 17408, torch.bfloat16))
+
+    def test_rejects_unsupported_dtype_and_shape(self):
+        self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 4096, 1024, torch.float16))
+        # k must be a multiple of BLOCK_K, n a multiple of BLOCK_N.
+        self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 4096, 1000, torch.bfloat16))
+        self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 4100, 1024, torch.bfloat16))
+        # split_k == 1 has no occupancy problem to fix.
+        self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 4096, 512, torch.bfloat16))
+
+    def test_rejects_other_arches(self):
+        with mock.patch.object(splitk, "is_gfx1151_supported", return_value=False):
+            self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 4096, 1024, torch.bfloat16))
+
+    def test_env_var_disables_the_path(self):
+        with mock.patch.object(splitk, "_is_disabled", return_value=True):
+            self.assertFalse(splitk.use_rdna_splitk_gemv(1, 4096, 1024, torch.bfloat16))
+

+@unittest.skipUnless(is_hip(), "the split-K GEMV path is only wired up on ROCm")
+class TestKernel(CustomTestCase):
+    def _run_case(self, n, k, seed=0):
+        torch.manual_seed(seed)
+        x = torch.randn(1, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        w = torch.randn(n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.05
+        out = splitk.rdna_splitk_gemv(x, w)
+        ref = x.float() @ w.float().t()
+        blas = (x @ w.t()).float()
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (1, n))
+        self.assertEqual(out.dtype, torch.bfloat16)
+        err = (out.float() - ref).abs().max().item()
+        err_blas = (blas - ref).abs().max().item()
+        # One bf16 ulp at the output scale: the error both paths can reach from the
+        # final store alone, and it grows with sqrt(K) for the accumulated part.
+        step = max(ref.abs().max().item() * 2**-9, 1e-6)
+        self.assertLess(err, 10 * step, (n, k, err, step))
+        # fp32 accumulation is at least as accurate as rocBLAS bf16 output.
+        self.assertLessEqual(err, err_blas * 2 + 1e-3, (n, k, err, err_blas))
+        self.assertFalse(torch.isnan(out).any().item(), (n, k))
+
+    def test_decode_shapes(self):
+        for n, k in DECODE_SHAPES:
+            with self.subTest(n=n, k=k):
+                self._run_case(n, k)
+
+    def test_large_model_shapes(self):
+        # Qwen3.5-4B / Qwen3.8-27B dense shapes, including a split_k=34 down_proj.
+        for n, k in [(10240, 2560), (18432, 2560), (2560, 9216), (5120, 17408)]:
+            with self.subTest(n=n, k=k):
+                self._run_case(n, k)
+
+    def test_batch_invariant(self):
+        """Same output regardless of what else is in flight."""
+        torch.manual_seed(1)
+        x = torch.randn(1, 1024, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        w = torch.randn(4096, 1024, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.05
+        a = splitk.rdna_splitk_gemv(x, w)
+        splitk.rdna_splitk_gemv(
+            torch.randn(1, 2048, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"),
+            torch.randn(1024, 2048, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.05,
+        )
+        b = splitk.rdna_splitk_gemv(x, w)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(a, b))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
